'''Michael Albeck''' ([[Hebrew language|Hebrew]]: מיכאל אלבק; born October 1934) is an Israeli [[Organic chemistry|organic]] and [[Bioorganic chemistry|bioorganic]] chemist of [[:Category:Tellurium compounds|tellurium compounds]]. He was President of [[Bar-Ilan University]] from 1986 to 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=6551&pt=1&pid=988&level=5&cPath=35,983,988 |title=Bar-Ilan Presidents &#124; Bar Ilan University |publisher=.biu.ac.il |date= |accessdate=2020-02-14}}</ref>

==Early life and education ==
Michael Albeck was born in Berlin, Germany to [[Hanoch Albeck|Hanoch]] and Henya Albeck in October 1934. His family immigrated to [[Mandatory Palestine]] in 1935 and settled in [[Jerusalem]]. He earned both MSc in Chemistry (1959) and PhD (1962) from The [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]].   

== Career ==
He worked as Principal Investigator in the Institute for Fiber and Forest Products in Jerusalem in 1962-1964, as the head of the chemical laboratories of [[Mekorot|Mekorot Water Company]] in 1964-1965, and then he joined [[Bar Ilan University]]<ref>[http://ch.biu.ac.il/faculty Department of Chemistry, Bar Ilan University]</ref> as a faculty member at the Department of Chemistry, becoming a Full Professor in 1978. Albeck served as the [[Dean (education)|Dean]] of The Faculty of Natural Sciences<ref>[http://esc.biu.ac.il//en Faculty of Exact Sciences, BIU]</ref>  of Bar Ilan University twice (1967-1969 and 1972-1975), as a member of the Board of Governors and the Board of Trustees of the university<ref>[http://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=1080&pt=1&pid=983&level=4&cPath=35,983,1080 Bar Ilan Board of Trustees]</ref> (1982-1999) and as the university’s [[Rector (academia)|Rector]] (1982-1986) and [[Chancellor (education)|President]]<ref>{{Cite web |title=Bar-Ilan University - BIU {{!}} Israel |url=https://www.biu.ac.il/en?id=6551&pt=1&pid=988&level=5&cPath=35,983,988 |access-date=2025-05-21 |website=www.biu.ac.il}}</ref> (1986-1989; succeeding [[Emanuel Rackman]], and succeeded by [[Ernest Krausz]]).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www1.biu.ac.il/indexE.php?id=6551&pt=1&pid=988&level=5&cPath=35,983,988 |title=Bar-Ilan Presidents &#124; Bar Ilan University |publisher=.biu.ac.il |date= |accessdate=2020-02-18}}</ref> Since 2003, he is a Professor Emeritus at Bar Ilan. 

Albeck assumed many scientific duties outside Bar Ilan University, including member of the boards of The Weizmann Scientific Press, [[Dead Sea Works]], The German-Israel Binational Foundation (GIF),<ref>[http://www.gif.org.il/Pages/default.aspx The German-Israeli Foundation for Scientific Research and Development (GIF)]</ref> [[Teva Pharmaceutical Industries|Teva Pharmaceuticals]], and as the President of The [[Israel Chemical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=ICSThe Israel Chemical Society |url=https://www.chemistry.org.il/ |access-date=2025-05-21 |language=en-US}}</ref> Albeck is the son of the late Prof. [[Hanoch Albeck]], who was a Professor of [[Talmud]] at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] and one of the foremost scholars of [[Jewish studies|Judaic studies]]. Michael and his wife Shulamit, a retired Faculty member of the School of Social Work at Bar Ilan University, have four children, including chemistry professor [[Amnon Albeck]], grandchildren and great grandchildren.

==Scientific interests and publications==
Albeck’s main scientific interests are in the chemistry<ref>''Synthesis''  '''1989''', ''8'', ''635'', [[DOI:10.1055/s-1989-27344]]; 
''Inorg. Chem.'' '''1998''', ''37'', ''1704'', [[DOI:10.1021/ic971456t]]; 
''ChemMedChem'' '''2007''', ''2'', ''1601'', [[DOI:10.1002/cmdc.200700155]].</ref> and biological activity<ref>''Nature''  '''1987''', ''330'', ''173'', [[DOI:10.1038/330173a0]]; 
''Nat. Immun. Cell Growth Regul.'' '''1990''', ''9'', ''182''; 
''Cancer Res.'' '''1991''', ''51'', ''1499'', available at http://cancerres.aacrjournals.org/content/51/5/1499.full.pdf+html;
''Nat. Immunol.''  '''1993''', ''12'', ''50'';
''J. Neurochem.''  '''2003''', ''85'', ''90'';
''Virus Res.''  '''2012''', ''166'', ''68'', [[DOI:10.1016/j.virusres.2012.03.004]];
''Cancer Res.''  '''2014''', ''74'', ''3092'', [[DOI:10.1158/0008-5472.CAN-13-2159]].</ref> of organic and inorganic [[:Category:Tellurium compounds|tellurium compounds]]. Two of these [[Chemical compound|compounds]], AS101 and SAS, exhibit [[Immunomodulator|immuno-modulating]], antiviral and anticancer activity. They are now in various [[clinical trial]]s. He published over 120 scientific publications and patents.
